PASS on the fake backend only; the package is model-authored and unreviewed, no hardware was attached and the upstream environment was never imported or run. The upstream MazeEnvSample5x5 needs gym, pygame and numpy (setup.py:12) and its constructor enables the pygame path (maze_env.py:16-37, maze_view_2d.py:14-16), so the fake is a pure-Python re-implementation of the MazeEnv/MazeView2D grid rules that embeds the shipped 5x5 wall layout as test data; it was not compared with a real upstream run. Only the fixed maze-v0 5x5 sample environment is served; the random, portal and loop variants are not modelled. NOT COVERED: the rgb_array/pygame rendering (cap.world.render.v1 stays unbound) and the exact numpy int64 observation type (the fake returns plain lists). The fake emulates the 2000-step TimeLimit that gym.make adds to maze-v0 (gym_maze/__init__.py:7); the raw MazeEnv.step returns the legacy four-tuple and never truncates. The seed is accepted and echoed but does not change the fixed sample maze because MazeEnv.seed's generator is unused by reset and step. The action bound 0..3 is the bridge-derived Discrete(4) from the fake's action space; no Limit is declared and no operator_required bound exists. Warnings are the expected bridge residuals: G6.NO_NATIVE_CALL for cap.world.seed.v1 (the seed only sets the seed of the next reset, so it makes no native call) and four G8.NO_UNIT for the bridge-derived integer inputs (ticks, action.index, seed twice); there are no G4.REF_VALUE or G4.REF_BINARY warnings. Mock path: a package fake rather than the upstream simulator because package code may not import or run the read-only clone and the upstream constructor needs pygame; the sim backend name would go through the bridge's gymnasium/gym make and was not run. DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: none; GymnasiumDriver expresses the legacy gym reset/step shapes through the bridge. No extension capability ids were used, so there are no catalogue_requests.
